A FRIENDLY CONTEST OF INSTINCTS

Meet on the sumo table.

No injuries. No lost beetles.

Choose two beetles and watch them try to push each other out. Each body and brain brings a different strategy.

LEAF & LINEAGESUMO TABLE
Red cornerBlue corner
0:00

Closer to the center wins when time runs out.

The table is ready. Choose your beetles.

Push the other beetle’s center over the white line to win immediately. At 60 seconds, the beetle closest to the center wins; only an equal-distance finish is a tie. If both cross the line in the same instant, the closer beetle wins. The circles are distance guides, not separate point zones. Playback speed changes the animation, not the result.

Different routes to a good push

A front push meets bracing. Side pushes test sideways balance; rear pushes test recovery. Mass and grip resist sliding, but a heavy beetle accelerates and turns more slowly.

Tracking, reaction speed, focus and ring tactics help find a useful angle. Pushing and wandering instincts can pull in opposite directions. Endurance matters in a long contest.

Battle together on two computers

Host: choose a red-corner beetle and create a code. Your classmate chooses their own red-corner beetle, enters your code, and joins as blue. Once both are ready, the host presses Start shared match. Both screens use a shared countdown, matching moves and the same winner. The winner dances under confetti. Keep both screens open; a returning screen catches up. Small visual timing differences can occur on slow connections. Only the selected anonymous beetle is shared. Codes expire after two hours.

    THE POCKET FIELD GUIDE
    Make the beetle you imagine.
    Choose, breed, discover
    Click a beetle for a large view, then add it to a jar. You can also drag a tank beetle into a jar slot. Put two to four different beetles in a jar, check “Use this jar,” and breed. One jar produces 10–20 babies. Two jars split that same total; an odd extra goes randomly to either. Each baby gets two distinct parents chosen randomly inside its own jar. Two parents in a jar keep that cross exclusive. Original parents stay until you remove them.
    A quiet, living tank
    Beetles wander after birth. Drag a beetle to place it. Holding pauses only that beetle; opening its information leaves the others moving. Cool & pause freezes both tanks with a brief pretend mist; Run resumes movement. Cooling, bedding, decoration and movement do not change genes or breeding chances. There are no birds, hunger or automatic mating. The optional sumo table is a harmless pushing contest. Inherited speed changes walking pace, while strength is a fictional relative trait, not a fertility advantage. The short field-mark tags are consistent clues; discover their meaning through observation and breeding. In sumo, muscle force drives a sustained push; speed helps approaching and circling. Strength, grip, stamina, attention and position can all matter.
    Genes that can hide
    The model stores 80 paired records on seven chromosome pairs. Colors, markings, finish and categorical forms have two inherited copies. Continuous anatomy and behavior are breeding-value estimates representing many small genetic effects. A baby gets a contribution from each actual parent. Color, pattern and categorical forms transmit actual parental copies, including hidden variants. Overall body size combines inherited length and width as a continuous measurement, without small/medium/large tiers. Students can track it in the raw data notebook. Size dimensions, speed-related values, stamina, strength, continuous appendage dimensions, and behavior usually stay close to the parents’ averages, with small variation in either direction. Rare larger mutations can make a bigger change. Linked copies usually travel together; a crossover can exchange sections. A dominant S suppressor hides marks. Only ss reveals them; a separate T gate limits visible patterns to one color, while tt allows two. Both hidden colors and placement genes still pass on. Two Ss Tt parents with mutation off can produce plain, one-color and two-color offspring. Small broods need not match average odds.
    Eighty inherited traits
    Body and pattern colors, mark size and distribution, symmetry, antenna frameworks, fine hairs, leg forms, motor speed and strength all have their own inherited copies. Frameworks can mask modifiers. Continuous physical and behavior traits use a quantitative breeding model, so they do not flip between a parent’s widely different hidden values. Colors and pattern genes can still reveal inherited surprises. The stronger expression copy selects a categorical framework or pigment recipe; numeric copies average when expressed. Quantitative contributions are formed near each parent’s expressed value before mutation, rather than choosing a single large-effect allele. No antenna or color is universally better. Stable developmental variation gives each baby a fixed pattern; inspecting, cooling or resizing never rerolls it.
    From tiny to extravagant
    Antennae include threads, beads, bristles, clubs, sawteeth, single and double combs, fans, leaf plates, elbows, plumes and side bristles. Length, width, segments, branching, fine hair and spread vary too. These mix beetle and other insect inspirations for creative play; they are not a species identification tool. Legs keep three pairs and can show runners, sturdy walkers, shovel forelegs, large hind thighs, paddles, hooks, spines and long toes.
    Keep a family
    The tank holds at most 48 beetles. Choose whether tank and nursery keep the newest brood only or the two newest broods; the starting group counts as a brood. A change takes effect when the next brood is born. Older unsaved beetles then leave automatically, while their trait measurements remain in the notebook. Keep up to ten favorites in the separate top-down Keep tank, return others to the breeder tank, and select descendants for later crosses. Save favorites before the next brood arrives. Keep tank beetles and jar parents are protected. The magnifying-glass button opens a dense technical report with all 80 paired genetic records, both copies, full-precision expression values, mutation flags, expression gates and derived size/speed measurements. Teacher labs can always open it. In student links it follows Show all genetics. The report can be downloaded or printed. Named beetles show upright name tags in both tanks and are automatically excluded from cleanup. Inspect a beetle to toggle Exclude from cleanup. Exclusions stay with the saved tank, are not inherited, and do not use a Keep tank slot. Clear unsaved beetles opens a review list; check exclusions and confirm which beetles to delete. Cancel changes nothing. Family labels and measured trait data remain after deletion. Brood rounds count crossings; lineage generation follows actual ancestry. Repeated broods of the same parents are siblings.
    Trade with a classmate
    Choose a beetle outside the jars and create a trade code. Your friend enters the code and offers a beetle back. Preview both, then the code creator confirms the one-for-one swap. Either student can cancel first. Keep using the original tank and device until finished. Trades need internet and device storage. Codes for the sumo table are separate; battles never move your beetles.
    Collect trait data
    Open the trait notebook to choose a measurement such as walking speed, stamina or antenna length. Read the raw data table across lineage generations or breeding rounds, filter by jar, and download the selected individual measurements as CSV. Archived measurements remain after beetles leave the tank; older missing records are marked unavailable. Strength and hidden gene copies are excluded from the notebook even when full statistics are enabled.
    Save your work
    The lab auto-saves locally when available and automatically reopens your last tank for this class link on this browser and device. New tank is a separate, confirmed choice. Different class links have separate saves. Save tank file downloads a portable copy including all genes, jar groups, names and notes. Open tank file restores it. Shared class links start a fresh tank with the same founders and permissions; they do not contain your later offspring. On shared school devices, save a file before leaving. This original model teaches inheritance and is not a claim about actual beetle genetics.
